expected:
# B2 — two sides of one link report different lldpRemPortIdSubtype forms for the peer port
Expected: read-time normalization (normalizePortName(), ported from the G-model, §5.4) means
"GigabitEthernet0/24" (ifDescr-style, remote_port_desc present) and "Gi0/24" (short ifName
form) normalize to the same value and the two sides collapse to ONE link, not two. Already
partially demonstrated live in t-model-findings.md (Switch1's peer.port normalized to gi0/0 for
its Router1 link) — this test constructs the (ifName vs macAddress vs local subtype) cases
explicitly via hand-built blobs rather than relying on what the lab's fixture happened to send.
actual: Two UNMERGED half-links form, not one: h1's side reports its peer port as the raw MAC ('aa:00:00:00:0b:02', per resolvePortLabel's macAddress-subtype branch returning the MAC verbatim -- ported faithfully from the G-model's own resolvePortLabel, same limitation there), which never matches h2's REAL port name ('GigabitEthernet0/2') because far-port resolution (buildLinks()) only matches by normalized NAME, never by MAC, even though the peer's own port.mac IS available in ports_by_hostid. The port-conflict detector DOES correctly notice two links now claim h1's port and flags the second one conflict=true -- so the failure is visible in diagnostics, not silent, but the result is still two half-links instead of one clean merged link.
proposed_uc_verdict: B2's ✅ holds for ifName/local-with-desc forms but not for the macAddress-subtype-only case, which is a real, narrower gap worth its own line.
notes: Not fixed (ground rule 1). A real fix would add a MAC-based fallback match in buildLinks()'s far-port resolution when the peer_port_raw looks like a MAC and the peer cluster's ports include a matching port.mac.
